[gs_2024_7_P296_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P296 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview
The three lines of defense structure promotes the accountability of first line risk takers, provides a framework for effective challenge by the second line and empowers independent review from the third line.

[gs_2024_7_P297_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P297 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Processes.

[gs_2024_7_P297_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P297 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We maintain various processes that are critical components of our risk management framework, including (i) risk identification and assessment, (ii) risk appetite, limits, thresholds and alerts, (iii) control monitoring and testing, and (iv) risk reporting.

[gs_2024_7_P297_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P297 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• Risk Identification and Assessment. We believe the identification and assessment of our risks is a critical step in providing our Board and senior management transparency and insight into the range and materiality of our risks. We have a comprehensive data collection process, including firmwide policies and procedures that require all employees to report and escalate risk events. Our approach for risk identification and assessment is comprehensive across all risk types, is dynamic and forward-looking to reflect and adapt to our changing risk profile and business environment, leverages subject matter expertise, and allows for prioritization of our most critical risks. We perform risk assessments periodically with the aim of ensuring that our material financial and nonfinancial risks are mitigated through controls to an acceptable tolerance level in accordance with our risk appetite. Our risk assessments include, among other things, the use of stress testing as well as an assessment of our internal control processes designed to mitigate such risks.

[gs_2024_7_P298_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P298 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Firmwide stress testing is an important part of our risk management process.

[gs_2024_7_P298_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P298 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
It allows us to quantify our exposure to tail risks, highlight potential loss concentrations, undertake risk/reward analysis, and assess and mitigate our risk positions.

[gs_2024_7_P298_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P298 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Firmwide stress tests are performed on a regular basis and are designed to ensure a comprehensive analysis of our vulnerabilities and idiosyncratic risks combining financial and nonfinancial risks, including, but not limited to, credit, market, liquidity and funding, operational and compliance, strategic, systemic and emerging risks into our stress scenarios.

[gs_2024_7_P298_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P298 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We also perform ad hoc stress tests in anticipation of market events or conditions.

[gs_2024_7_P298_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P298 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Stress tests are also used to assess capital adequacy as part of our capital planning and stress testing process.

[gs_2024_7_P298_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P298 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
See "Capital Management and Regulatory Capital - Capital Management" for further information.

[gs_2024_7_P299_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P299 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We maintain a daily discipline of marking substantially all of our inventory to current market levels.

[gs_2024_7_P299_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P299 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We carry our inventory at fair value, with changes in valuation reflected immediately in our risk management systems and in net revenues.

[gs_2024_7_P299_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P299 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We do so because we believe this discipline is one of the most effective tools for assessing and managing risk and that it provides transparent and realistic insight into our inventory exposures.

[gs_2024_7_P299_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P299 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• Risk Appetite, Limits, Thresholds and Alerts. We apply risk limits, thresholds and alerts to control and monitor risk across transactions, products, businesses and markets. The Board, directly or indirectly through its Risk Committee, approves limits, thresholds and alerts included in our risk appetite statement at firmwide, business and product levels. In addition, the Firmwide Risk Appetite Committee, through delegated authority from the Firmwide Enterprise Risk Committee, is responsible for approving our risk limits, thresholds and alerts policy, subject to the overall limits directly or indirectly approved by the Board, and monitoring these limits.

[gs_2024_7_P300_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P300 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
The Firmwide Risk Appetite Committee is responsible for approving and monitoring limits at firmwide, business and product levels.

[gs_2024_7_P300_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P300 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Certain limits may be set at levels that will require periodic adjustment, rather than at levels that reflect our maximum risk appetite.

[gs_2024_7_P300_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P300 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
This fosters an ongoing dialogue about risk among our first and second lines of defense, committees and senior management, as well as rapid escalation of risk-related matters.

[gs_2024_7_P300_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P300 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
The Firmwide Risk Appetite Committee also authorizes Risk to set limits and thresholds to support monitoring and oversight at a more granular level.

[gs_2024_7_P300_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P300 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
For example, Market Risk sets limits at certain product and desk levels, and Credit Risk sets limits for individual counterparties and their subsidiaries, industries and countries.

[gs_2024_7_P300_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P300 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Limits are reviewed regularly and amended on a permanent or temporary basis to reflect changes to our strategic business plan, as well as changing market conditions, business conditions or risk tolerance.

[gs_2024_7_P300_S007] Parent gs_2024_7_P300 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Risks limits are monitored by the respective Risk functions.

[gs_2024_7_P301_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P301 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• Control Monitoring and Testing.We perform control monitoring and testing to measure the effectiveness of our key controls and to ensure that we are in compliance with policies, codes of conduct, control standards and regulatory requirements. Monitoring and testing is performed by dedicated teams within the first and second lines of defense. These teams establish procedures, develop risk-based annual plans, perform control testing and escalate identified issues. Issues identified by the dedicated teams, as well as self-identified issues by our employees, are assessed for appropriate escalation and resolution. Where material or thematic issues exist, we develop a plan to remediate them, as appropriate, and monitor the remediation activities.

[gs_2024_7_P301_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P301 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• Risk Reporting. Effective risk reporting depends on our ability to get the right information to the right people at the right time. Risk reporting is designed to be both forward- and backward-looking and consider detailed information on existing and emerging risk exposures. Risk reporting may include stress testing and scenario analysis, information about the risk profiles for financial and nonfinancial risks, utilization of risk limits and thresholds, details of new and emerging risks identified through our risk identification processes, details of issues, significant internal and external events, and information related to the effectiveness of our controls and remediation plans. As such, we focus on the rigor and effectiveness of our risk systems, with the objective of ensuring that our risk management technology systems provide us with complete, accurate and timely information. Our risk reporting process is designed to take into account information about both existing and emerging risks, thereby enabling our risk committees and senior management to perform their responsibilities with the appropriate level of insight into risk exposures. We make extensive use of risk committees and councils that meet regularly and serve as an important means to facilitate and foster ongoing discussions to manage and mitigate risks. We maintain strong and proactive communication about risk and we have a culture of collaboration in decision-making among our first and second lines of defense, committees and senior management. While our first line of defense is accountable and responsible for management of their risk, we dedicate extensive resources to our second line of defense in order to reinforce the importance of having effective oversight and challenge, and a strong culture of escalation and accountability across all functions.

[gs_2024_7_P302_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P302 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
People.

[gs_2024_7_P302_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P302 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Even the best technology serves only as a tool for helping to make informed decisions in real time about the risks we are taking.

[gs_2024_7_P302_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P302 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Ultimately, effective risk management requires our people to interpret our risk data on an ongoing and timely basis and adjust risk positions accordingly.

[gs_2024_7_P302_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P302 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
The experience of our professionals, and their understanding of the nuances and limitations of each risk measure, guides us in assessing exposures and maintaining them within prudent levels.

[gs_2024_7_P303_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P303 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We reinforce a culture of effective risk management, consistent with our risk appetite, in our training and development programs, as well as in the way we evaluate performance, and recognize and reward our people.

[gs_2024_7_P303_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P303 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES

[gs_2024_7_P303_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P303 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
As part of our performance review process, we assess reputational excellence, including how an employee exercises good risk management and reputational judgment, and adheres to our code of conduct and compliance policies.

[gs_2024_7_P303_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P303 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Our review and reward processes are designed to communicate and reinforce to our professionals the link between behavior and how people are recognized, the need to focus on our clients and our reputation, and the need to always act in accordance with our highest standards.

Additionally, the Firmwide Enterprise Risk Committee performs enhanced reviews of significant risk events, the top residual and emerging risks, and the overall risk and control environment in each of our business units in order to propose uplifts, identify elements that are common to all business units and analyze the consolidated residual risks that we face.

[gs_2024_7_P309_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P309 - Item 7 - Overview and Structure of Risk Management > Structure

The Firmwide Risk Appetite Committee (through delegated authority from the Firmwide Enterprise Risk Committee) is responsible for the ongoing approval and monitoring of risk frameworks, policies and parameters related to our risk management processes, as well as limits, thresholds and alerts, at firmwide, business and product levels. To assist the Firmwide Risk Appetite Committee in carrying out its mandate, a number of other risk committees with dedicated oversight for stress testing, model risks, Volcker Rule compliance, as well as our investments or other capital commitments that may give rise to financial risk, report into the Firmwide Risk Appetite Committee. [gs_2024_7_P312_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P312 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Overview
Liquidity risk is the risk that we will be unable to fund ourselves or meet our liquidity needs in the event of firm-specific, broader industry or market liquidity stress events.

[gs_2024_7_P312_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P312 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Overview
We have in place a comprehensive and conservative set of liquidity and funding policies.

[gs_2024_7_P312_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P312 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Overview
Our principal objective is to be able to fund ourselves and to enable our core businesses to continue to serve clients and generate revenues, even under adverse circumstances.

[gs_2024_7_P313_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P313 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Overview
Corporate Treasury is responsible for our liquidity, including developing and executing our liquidity and funding strategy.

[gs_2024_7_P314_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P314 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Overview
Liquidity Risk, which is part of our second line of defense and reports to our chief risk officer, has primary responsibility for assessing, monitoring and managing our liquidity risk by providing independent firmwide oversight and challenge across our global businesses.

[gs_2024_7_P314_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P314 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Overview
Liquidity Risk is also responsible for the establishment of stress testing and limits frameworks.

[gs_2024_7_P315_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P315 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Overview > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES


[gs_2024_7_P316_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P316 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
We manage liquidity risk according to three principles: (i) hold sufficient excess liquidity in the form of GCLA to cover outflows during a stressed period, (ii) maintain appropriate Asset-Liability Management and (iii) maintain a viable Contingency Funding Plan.

[gs_2024_7_P317_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P317 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
GCLA.

[gs_2024_7_P317_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P317 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
GCLA is liquidity that we maintain to meet a broad range of potential cash outflows and collateral needs in a stressed environment.

[gs_2024_7_P317_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P317 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
A primary liquidity principle is to pre-fund our estimated potential cash and collateral needs during a liquidity crisis and hold this liquidity in the form of unencumbered, highly liquid securities and cash.

[gs_2024_7_P317_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P317 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
We believe that the securities held in our GCLA would be readily convertible to cash in a matter of days, through liquidation, by entering into repurchase agreements or from maturities of resale agreements, and that this cash would allow us to meet immediate obligations without needing to sell other assets or depend on additional funding from credit-sensitive markets.

[gs_2024_7_P318_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P318 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
Our GCLA reflects the following principles:

[gs_2024_7_P318_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P318 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
• The first days or weeks of a liquidity crisis are the most critical to a company's survival;

[gs_2024_7_P318_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P318 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
• Focus must be maintained on all potential cash and collateral outflows, not just disruptions to financing flows. Our businesses are diverse, and our liquidity needs are determined by many factors, including market movements, collateral requirements and client commitments, all of which can change dramatically in a difficult funding environment;

[gs_2024_7_P318_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P318 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
• During a liquidity crisis, credit-sensitive funding, including unsecured debt, certain deposits and some types of secured financing agreements, may be unavailable, and the terms (e.g., interest rates, collateral provisions and tenor) or availability of other types of secured financing may change and certain deposits may be withdrawn; and

[gs_2024_7_P318_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P318 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
• As a result of our policy to pre-fund liquidity that we estimate may be needed in a crisis, we hold more unencumbered securities and have larger funding balances than our businesses would otherwise require. We believe that our liquidity is stronger with greater balances of highly liquid unencumbered securities, even though it increases our total assets and our funding costs.

[gs_2024_7_P319_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P319 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
We maintain our GCLA across Group Inc., Goldman Sachs Funding LLC (Funding IHC) and Group Inc.'s major broker-dealer and bank subsidiaries, asset types and clearing agents with the goal of providing us with sufficient operating liquidity to ensure timely settlement in all major markets, even in a difficult funding environment.

[gs_2024_7_P319_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P319 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
In addition to the GCLA, we maintain cash balances and securities in several of our other entities, primarily for use in specific currencies, entities or jurisdictions where we do not have immediate access to parent company liquidity.

[gs_2024_7_P320_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P320 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
Asset-Liability Management.

[gs_2024_7_P320_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P320 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
Our liquidity risk management policies are designed to ensure we have a sufficient amount of financing, even when funding markets experience persistent stress.

[gs_2024_7_P320_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P320 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
We manage the maturities and diversity of our funding across markets, products and counterparties, and seek to maintain a diversified funding profile with an appropriate tenor, taking into consideration the characteristics and liquidity profile of our assets.

[gs_2024_7_P321_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P321 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
Our approach to asset-liability management includes:

[gs_2024_7_P321_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P321 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
• Conservatively managing the overall characteristics of our funding book, with a focus on maintaining long-term, diversified sources of funding in excess of our current requirements. See "Balance Sheet and Funding Sources - Funding Sources" for further information;

[gs_2024_7_P321_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P321 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
• Actively managing and monitoring our asset base, with particular focus on the liquidity, holding period and ability to fund assets on a secured basis. We assess our funding requirements and our ability to liquidate assets in a stressed environment while appropriately managing risk. This enables us to determine the most appropriate funding products and tenors. See "Balance Sheet and Funding Sources - Balance Sheet Management" for further information about our balance sheet management process and "- Funding Sources - Secured Funding" for further information about asset classes that may be harder to fund on a secured basis; and

[gs_2024_7_P321_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P321 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
• Raising secured and unsecured financing that has a long tenor relative to the liquidity profile of our assets. This reduces the risk that our liabilities will come due in advance of our ability to generate liquidity from the sale of our assets. Because we maintain a highly liquid balance sheet, the holding period of certain of our assets may be materially shorter than their contractual maturity dates.

[gs_2024_7_P322_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P322 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
Our goal is to ensure that we maintain sufficient liquidity to fund our assets and meet our contractual and contingent obligations in normal times, as well as during periods of market stress.

[gs_2024_7_P322_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P322 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
Through our dynamic balance sheet management process, we use actual and projected asset balances to determine secured and unsecured funding requirements.

[gs_2024_7_P322_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P322 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
Funding plans are reviewed and approved by the Firmwide Asset Liability Committee.

[gs_2024_7_P322_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P322 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
In addition, Risk and the Firmwide Asset Liability Committee review our total unsecured long-term borrowings and total shareholders' equity to help ensure that we maintain a level of long-term funding that is sufficient to meet our long-term financing requirements.

[gs_2024_7_P322_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P322 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
In a liquidity crisis, we would begin by liquidating and monetizing our GCLA before selling other assets.

[gs_2024_7_P322_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P322 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles
However, we recognize that orderly asset sales may be prudent or necessary in a severe or persistent liquidity crisis.

[gs_2024_7_P323_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P323 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES


[gs_2024_7_P324_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P324 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
The majority of our unsecured borrowings is raised by Group Inc., which provides the necessary funds to Funding IHC and other subsidiaries, some of which are regulated, to meet their asset financing, liquidity and capital requirements.

[gs_2024_7_P324_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P324 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
In addition, Group Inc. provides its regulated subsidiaries with the necessary capital to meet their regulatory requirements.

[gs_2024_7_P324_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P324 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
The benefits of this approach to subsidiary funding are enhanced control and greater flexibility to meet the funding requirements of our subsidiaries.

[gs_2024_7_P324_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P324 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
Funding is also raised at the subsidiary level through a variety of products, including deposits, secured funding and unsecured borrowings.

[gs_2024_7_P325_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P325 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
Our intercompany funding policies assume that a subsidiary's funds or securities are not freely available to its parent, Funding IHC or other subsidiaries unless (i) legally provided for and (ii) there are no additional regulatory, tax or other restrictions.

[gs_2024_7_P325_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P325 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
In particular, many of our subsidiaries are subject to laws that authorize regulatory bodies to block or reduce the flow of funds from those subsidiaries to Group Inc. or Funding IHC.

[gs_2024_7_P325_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P325 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
Regulatory action of that kind could impede access to funds that Group Inc. needs to make payments on its obligations.

[gs_2024_7_P325_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P325 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
Accordingly, we assume that the capital provided to our regulated subsidiaries is not available to Group Inc. or other subsidiaries and any other financing provided to our regulated subsidiaries is not available to Group Inc. or Funding IHC until the maturity of such financing.

[gs_2024_7_P326_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P326 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
Group Inc. has provided substantial amounts of equity and subordinated indebtedness, directly or indirectly, to its regulated subsidiaries.

[gs_2024_7_P326_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P326 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
For example, as of December 2024, Group Inc. had $38.69 billion of equity and subordinated indebtedness invested in GS&Co., its principal U.S. registered broker-dealer; $47.21 billion invested in GSI, a regulated U.K. broker-dealer; $2.08 billion invested in GSJCL, a regulated Japanese broker-dealer; $62.81 billion invested in GS Bank USA, a regulated New York State-chartered bank; and $5.30 billion invested in GSIB, a regulated U.K. bank.

[gs_2024_7_P326_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P326 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
Group Inc. also provides financing, directly or indirectly, in the form of: $131.82 billion of unsubordinated loans (including secured loans of $59.97 billion) and $32.92 billion of collateral and cash deposits to these entities as of December 2024.

[gs_2024_7_P326_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P326 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
In addition, as of December 2024, Group Inc. had significant amounts of capital invested in and loans to its other regulated subsidiaries.

[gs_2024_7_P327_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P327 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
Contingency Funding Plan.

[gs_2024_7_P327_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P327 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
We maintain a contingency funding plan to provide a framework for analyzing and responding to a liquidity crisis situation or periods of market stress.

[gs_2024_7_P327_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P327 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
Our contingency funding plan outlines a list of potential risk factors, key reports and metrics that are reviewed on an ongoing basis to assist in assessing the severity of, and managing through, a liquidity crisis and/or market dislocation.

[gs_2024_7_P327_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P327 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
The contingency funding plan also describes in detail our potential responses if our assessments indicate that we have entered a liquidity crisis, which include pre-funding for what we estimate will be our potential cash and collateral needs, as well as utilizing secondary sources of liquidity.

[gs_2024_7_P327_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P327 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
Mitigants and action items to address specific risks which may arise are also described and assigned to individuals responsible for execution.

[gs_2024_7_P328_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P328 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Liquidity Risk Management Principles > Subsidiary Funding Policies
The contingency funding plan identifies key groups of individuals and their responsibilities, which include fostering effective coordination, control and distribution of information, implementing liquidity maintenance activities and managing internal and external communication, all of which are critical in the management of a crisis or period of market stress.

[gs_2024_7_P329_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P329 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Stress Tests
In order to determine the appropriate size of our GCLA, we model liquidity outflows over a range of scenarios and time horizons.

[gs_2024_7_P329_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P329 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Stress Tests
One of our primary internal liquidity risk models, referred to as the Modeled Liquidity Outflow, quantifies our liquidity risks over a 30-day stress scenario.

[gs_2024_7_P329_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P329 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Stress Tests
We also consider other factors, including, but not limited to, an assessment of our potential intraday liquidity needs through an additional internal liquidity risk model, referred to as the Intraday Liquidity Model, the results of our long-term stress testing models, our resolution liquidity models and other applicable regulatory requirements and a qualitative assessment of our condition, as well as the financial markets.

[gs_2024_7_P329_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P329 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Stress Tests
The results of the Modeled Liquidity Outflow, the Intraday Liquidity Model, the long-term stress testing models and the resolution liquidity models are reported to senior management on a regular basis.

[gs_2024_7_P329_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P329 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Stress Tests
We also perform firmwide stress tests.

[gs_2024_7_P329_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P329 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Stress Tests
See "Overview and Structure of Risk Management" for information about firmwide stress tests.

[gs_2024_7_P330_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P330 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Stress Tests > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Modeled Liquidity Outflow.

[gs_2024_7_P330_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P330 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Stress Tests > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Our Modeled Liquidity Outflow is based on conducting multiple scenarios that include combinations of market-wide and firm-specific stress.

[gs_2024_7_P330_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P330 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Stress Tests > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
These scenarios are characterized by the following qualitative elements:

[gs_2024_7_P330_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P330 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Stress Tests > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• Severely challenged market environments, which include low consumer and corporate confidence, financial and political instability, and adverse changes in market values, including potential declines in equity markets and widening of credit spreads; and

[gs_2024_7_P330_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P330 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Stress Tests > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES

[gs_2024_7_P331_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P331 - Item 7 - Liquidity Risk Management > Stress Tests > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• A combination of contractual outflows and contingent outflows arising from both our on- and off-balance sheet arrangements. Contractual outflows include, among other things, upcoming maturities of unsecured debt, term deposits and secured funding. Contingent outflows include, among other things, the withdrawal of customer credit balances in our prime brokerage business, increase in variation margin requirements due to adverse changes in the value of our exchange-traded and OTC-cleared derivatives, draws on unfunded commitments and withdrawals of deposits that have no contractual maturity. See notes to the consolidated financial statements for further information about contractual outflows, including Note 11 for collateralized financings, Note 13 for deposits, Note 14 for unsecured long-term borrowings and Note 15 for operating lease payments, and "Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements" for further information about our various types of off-balance sheet arrangements.

[gs_2024_7_P362_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P362 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Overview
Market risk is the risk of an adverse impact to our earnings due to changes in market conditions.

[gs_2024_7_P362_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P362 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Overview
Our assets and liabilities that give rise to market risk primarily include positions held for market making for our clients and for our investing and financing activities, and these positions change based on client demands and our investment opportunities.

[gs_2024_7_P362_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P362 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Overview
We employ a variety of risk measures, each described in the respective sections below, to monitor market risk.

[gs_2024_7_P362_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P362 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Overview
Categories of market risk include the following:

[gs_2024_7_P362_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P362 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Overview
• Interest rate risk: results from exposures to changes in the level, slope and curvature of yield curves, the volatilities of interest rates, prepayment speeds and credit spreads;

[gs_2024_7_P362_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P362 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Overview
• Equity price risk: results from exposures to changes in prices and volatilities of individual equities, baskets of equities and equity indices;

[gs_2024_7_P362_S007] Parent gs_2024_7_P362 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Overview
• Currency rate risk: results from exposures to changes in spot prices, forward prices and volatilities of currency rates; and

[gs_2024_7_P362_S008] Parent gs_2024_7_P362 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Overview
• Commodity price risk: results from exposures to changes in spot prices, forward prices and volatilities of commodities, such as crude oil, petroleum products, natural gas, electricity, and precious and base metals.

[gs_2024_7_P363_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P363 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Overview
Market Risk, which is part of our second line of defense and reports to our chief risk officer, has primary responsibility for assessing, monitoring and managing our market risk by providing independent firmwide oversight and challenge across our global businesses.

[gs_2024_7_P364_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P364 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Overview
Managers in revenue-producing units, Corporate Treasury and Market Risk discuss market information, positions and estimated loss scenarios on an ongoing basis.

[gs_2024_7_P364_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P364 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Overview
Managers in revenue-producing units and Corporate Treasury are accountable for managing risk within prescribed limits.

[gs_2024_7_P364_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P364 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Overview
These managers have in-depth knowledge of their positions, markets and the instruments available to hedge their exposures.

[gs_2024_7_P365_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P365 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Market Risk Management Process
Our process for managing market risk includes the critical components of our risk management framework described in the "Overview and Structure of Risk Management," as well as the following:

[gs_2024_7_P365_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P365 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Market Risk Management Process
• Monitoring compliance with established market risk limits and reporting our exposures;

[gs_2024_7_P365_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P365 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Market Risk Management Process
• Diversifying exposures;

[gs_2024_7_P365_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P365 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Market Risk Management Process
• Controlling position sizes; and

[gs_2024_7_P365_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P365 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Market Risk Management Process
• Evaluating mitigants, such as economic hedges in related securities or derivatives.

[gs_2024_7_P366_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P366 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Market Risk Management Process
Our market risk management systems enable us to perform an independent calculation of Value-at-Risk (VaR), Earnings-at-Risk (EaR) and other stress measures, capture risk measures at individual position levels, attribute risk measures to individual risk factors of each position, report many different views of the risk measures (e.g., by desk, business, product type or entity) and produce ad hoc analyses in a timely manner.

[gs_2024_7_P367_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P367 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures
We produce risk measures and monitor them against established market risk limits.

[gs_2024_7_P367_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P367 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures
These measures reflect an extensive range of scenarios and the results are aggregated at product, business and firmwide levels.

[gs_2024_7_P368_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P368 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures
We use a variety of risk measures to estimate the size of potential losses for small, moderate and more extreme market moves over both short- and long-term time horizons.

[gs_2024_7_P368_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P368 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures
Our primary risk measures are VaR, EaR and other stress tests.

[gs_2024_7_P369_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P369 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures
Our risk reports detail key risks, drivers and changes for each desk and business, and are distributed daily to senior management of both our revenue-producing units and Risk.

[gs_2024_7_P370_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P370 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures
Value-at-Risk.

[gs_2024_7_P370_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P370 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures
VaR is the potential loss in value due to adverse market movements over a defined time horizon with a specified confidence level.

[gs_2024_7_P370_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P370 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures
For assets and liabilities included in VaR, see "Financial Statement Linkages to Market Risk Measures." We typically employ a one-day time horizon with a 95% confidence level.

[gs_2024_7_P370_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P370 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures
We use a single VaR model, which captures risks, including those related to interest rates, equity prices, currency rates and commodity prices.

[gs_2024_7_P370_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P370 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures
As such, VaR facilitates comparison across portfolios of different risk characteristics.

[gs_2024_7_P370_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P370 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures
VaR also captures the diversification of aggregated risk at the firmwide level.

[gs_2024_7_P371_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P371 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We are aware of the inherent limitations to VaR and therefore use a variety of risk measures in our market risk management process.

[gs_2024_7_P371_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P371 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Inherent limitations to VaR include:

[gs_2024_7_P371_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P371 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• VaR does not estimate potential losses over longer time horizons where moves may be extreme;

[gs_2024_7_P371_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P371 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• VaR does not take account of the relative liquidity of different risk positions; and

[gs_2024_7_P371_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P371 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• Previous moves in market risk factors may not produce accurate predictions of all future market moves.

[gs_2024_7_P372_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P372 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
To comprehensively capture our exposures and relevant risks in our VaR calculation, we use historical simulations with full valuation of market factors at the position level by simultaneously shocking the relevant market factors for that position.

[gs_2024_7_P372_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P372 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
These market factors include spot prices, credit spreads, funding spreads, yield curves, volatility and correlation, and are updated periodically based on changes in the composition of positions, as well as variations in market conditions.

[gs_2024_7_P372_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P372 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We sample from five years of historical data to generate the scenarios for our VaR calculation.

[gs_2024_7_P372_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P372 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
The historical data is weighted so that the relative importance of the data reduces over time.

[gs_2024_7_P372_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P372 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
This gives greater importance to more recent observations and reflects current asset volatilities, which improves the accuracy of our estimates of potential loss.

[gs_2024_7_P372_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P372 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
As a result, even if our positions included in VaR were unchanged, our VaR would increase with increasing market volatility and vice versa.

[gs_2024_7_P373_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P373 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Given its reliance on historical data, VaR is most effective in estimating risk exposures in markets in which there are no sudden fundamental changes or shifts in market conditions.

[gs_2024_7_P374_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P374 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Our VaR measure does not include:

[gs_2024_7_P374_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P374 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• Positions that are not accounted for at fair value, such as held-to-maturity securities and loans, deposits and unsecured borrowings that are accounted for at amortized cost;

[gs_2024_7_P374_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P374 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• Available-for-sale securities for which the related unrealized fair value gains and losses are included in accumulated other comprehensive income/(loss);

[gs_2024_7_P374_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P374 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• Positions that are best measured and monitored using sensitivity measures; and

[gs_2024_7_P374_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P374 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• The impact of changes in counterparty and our own credit spreads on derivatives, as well as changes in our own credit spreads on financial liabilities for which the fair value option was elected.

[gs_2024_7_P375_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P375 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We perform daily backtesting of our VaR model (i.e., comparing daily net revenues for positions included in VaR to the VaR measure calculated as of the prior business day) at the firmwide level and for each of our businesses and major regulated subsidiaries.

[gs_2024_7_P376_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P376 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Earnings-at-Risk.

[gs_2024_7_P376_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P376 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We manage our interest rate risk using the EaR metric.

[gs_2024_7_P376_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P376 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
EaR measures the estimated impact of changes in interest rates to our net revenues and preferred stock dividends over a defined time horizon.

[gs_2024_7_P376_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P376 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
EaR complements the VaR metric, which measures the impact of interest rate changes that have an immediate impact on the fair values of our assets and liabilities (i.e., mark-to-market changes).

[gs_2024_7_P376_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P376 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Our exposure to interest rate risk occurs due to a variety of factors, including, but not limited to:

[gs_2024_7_P376_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P376 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• Differences in maturity or repricing dates of assets, liabilities, preferred stock and certain off-balance sheet instruments.

[gs_2024_7_P376_S007] Parent gs_2024_7_P376 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• Differences in the amounts of assets, liabilities, preferred stock and certain off-balance sheet instruments with the same maturity or repricing dates.

[gs_2024_7_P376_S008] Parent gs_2024_7_P376 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
• Certain interest rate sensitive fees.

[gs_2024_7_P377_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P377 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Corporate Treasury manages the aggregated interest rate risk from all businesses using both cash and derivatives instruments, including available-for-sale and held-to-maturity securities and interest rate derivatives.

[gs_2024_7_P377_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P377 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We measure EaR over a one-year time horizon following a 100- and 200-basis point instantaneous parallel shock in both short- and long-term interest rates.

[gs_2024_7_P377_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P377 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
This sensitivity is calculated relative to a baseline market scenario, which takes into consideration, among other things, the market's expectation of forward rates, as well as our expectation of future business activity.

[gs_2024_7_P377_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P377 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
These scenarios include contractual elements of assets, liabilities, preferred stock, and certain off-balance sheet instruments, such as rates of interest, principal repayment schedules, maturity and reset dates, and any interest rate ceilings or floors, as well as assumptions with respect to our balance sheet size and composition, prepayment behavior and deposit repricing.

[gs_2024_7_P377_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P377 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Deposit repricing is captured by evaluating the change in deposit rate paid relative to the change in market rates (deposit beta) and we calibrate the deposit betas used in our models by using a number of factors, including observed historical behavior, future expectations, funding needs and the competitive landscape.

[gs_2024_7_P377_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P377 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We continuously monitor the performance of our key assumptions against observed behavior and regularly review their sensitivity on our risk metrics.

[gs_2024_7_P378_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P378 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We manage EaR with a goal to reduce potential volatility resulting from changes in interest rates so it remains within our EaR risk appetite.

[gs_2024_7_P378_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P378 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Our EaR scenario is regularly evaluated and updated, if necessary, to reflect changes in our business plans, market conditions and other macroeconomic factors.

[gs_2024_7_P378_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P378 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
While management uses the best information available to estimate EaR, actual results may differ materially as a result of, among other things, changes in the economic environment or assumptions used in the process.

[gs_2024_7_P378_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P378 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We also measure the sensitivity of the economic value of our equity (EVE) to changes in interest rates.

[gs_2024_7_P378_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P378 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Compared to EaR, EVE provides a longer-term measurement of the interest rate risk exposure, primarily on non-trading assets and liabilities, by capturing the net impact of changes in interest rates to the present value of their cash flows.

[gs_2024_7_P379_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P379 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Corporate Treasury is responsible for our aggregated interest rate risk, including assessing and monitoring EaR and EVE sensitivity, and interest rate risk stress tests and assumptions.

[gs_2024_7_P380_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P380 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Risk, which is part of our second line of defense and reports to our chief risk officer, has primary responsibility for assessing, monitoring and managing our interest rate risk (including EaR and EVE sensitivity) by providing independent firmwide oversight and challenge across our global businesses.

[gs_2024_7_P381_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P381 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Stress Testing.

[gs_2024_7_P381_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P381 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Stress testing is a method of determining the effect of various hypothetical stress scenarios.

[gs_2024_7_P381_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P381 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We use stress tests to examine risks of specific portfolios, as well as the potential impact of our significant risk exposures.

[gs_2024_7_P381_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P381 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We use a variety of stress testing techniques to calculate the potential loss from a wide range of market moves on our portfolios, including firmwide stress tests, sensitivity analysis and scenario analysis.

[gs_2024_7_P381_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P381 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
The results of our various stress tests are analyzed together for risk management purposes.

[gs_2024_7_P381_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P381 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
See "Overview and Structure of Risk Management" for information about firmwide stress tests.

[gs_2024_7_P382_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P382 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Sensitivity analysis is used to quantify the impact of a market move in a single risk factor across all positions (e.g., equity prices or credit spreads) using a variety of defined market shocks, ranging from those that could be expected over a one-day time horizon up to those that could take many months to occur.

[gs_2024_7_P382_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P382 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
We also use sensitivity analysis to quantify the impact of the default of any single entity, which captures the risk of large or concentrated exposures.

[gs_2024_7_P383_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P383 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Scenario analysis is used to quantify the impact of a specified event, including how the event impacts multiple risk factors simultaneously.

[gs_2024_7_P383_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P383 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
For example, for sovereign stress testing we calculate potential direct exposure associated with our sovereign positions, as well as the corresponding debt, equity and currency exposures associated with our non-sovereign positions that may be impacted by the sovereign distress.

[gs_2024_7_P383_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P383 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
When conducting scenario analysis, we often consider a number of possible outcomes for each scenario, ranging from moderate to severely adverse market impacts.

[gs_2024_7_P383_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P383 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
In addition, these stress tests are constructed using both historical events and forward-looking hypothetical scenarios.

[gs_2024_7_P384_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P384 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Unlike VaR measures, which have an implied probability because they are calculated at a specified confidence level, there may not be an implied probability that our stress testing scenarios will occur.

[gs_2024_7_P384_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P384 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Instead, stress testing is used to model both moderate and more extreme moves in underlying market factors.

[gs_2024_7_P384_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P384 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Risk Measures > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
When estimating potential loss, we generally assume that our positions cannot be reduced or hedged (although experience demonstrates that we are generally able to do so).

[gs_2024_7_P385_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P385 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Limits
We use market risk limits at various levels to manage the size of our market exposures.

[gs_2024_7_P385_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P385 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Limits
These limits are set based on VaR, EaR and on a range of stress tests relevant to our exposures.

[gs_2024_7_P385_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P385 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Limits
See "Overview and Structure of Risk Management" for information about the limit approval process.

[gs_2024_7_P386_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P386 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Limits
Limits are monitored by Corporate Treasury and Risk.

[gs_2024_7_P386_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P386 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Limits
Risk is responsible for identifying and escalating to senior management and/or the appropriate risk committee, on a timely basis, instances where limits have been exceeded (e.g., due to positional changes or changes in market conditions, such as increased volatilities or changes in correlations).

[gs_2024_7_P386_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P386 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Limits
Such instances are remediated by a reduction in the positions we hold and/or a temporary or permanent increase to the limit, if warranted.

[gs_2024_7_P387_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P387 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Metrics
We analyze VaR at the firmwide level and a variety of more detailed levels, including by risk category, business and region.

[gs_2024_7_P387_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P387 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Metrics

[gs_2024_7_P387_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P387 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Metrics

[gs_2024_7_P387_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P387 - Item 7 - Market Risk Management > Metrics

[gs_2024_7_P411_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P411 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Overview
Credit risk represents the potential for loss due to the default or deterioration in credit quality of a counterparty (e.g., an OTC derivatives counterparty or a borrower) or an issuer of securities or other instruments we hold.

[gs_2024_7_P411_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P411 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Overview
Our exposure to credit risk comes mostly from client transactions in OTC derivatives and loans and lending commitments.

[gs_2024_7_P411_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P411 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Overview
Credit risk also comes from cash placed with banks, securities financing transactions (i.e., resale and repurchase agreements and securities borrowing and lending activities) and customer and other receivables.

[gs_2024_7_P412_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P412 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Overview
Credit Risk, which is part of our second line of defense and reports to our chief risk officer, has primary responsibility for assessing, monitoring and managing our credit risk by providing independent firmwide oversight and challenge across our global businesses.

[gs_2024_7_P412_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P412 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Overview
In addition, we hold other positions that give rise to credit risk (e.g., bonds and secondary bank loans).

[gs_2024_7_P412_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P412 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Overview
These credit risks are captured as a component of market risk measures, which are monitored and managed by Market Risk.

[gs_2024_7_P412_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P412 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Overview
We also enter into derivatives to manage market risk exposures.

[gs_2024_7_P412_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P412 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Overview
Such derivatives also give rise to credit risk, which is monitored and managed by Credit Risk.

[gs_2024_7_P413_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P413 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
Our process for managing credit risk includes the critical components of our risk management framework described in the "Overview and Structure of Risk Management," as well as the following:

[gs_2024_7_P413_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P413 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
• Monitoring compliance with established credit risk limits and reporting our credit exposures and credit concentrations;

[gs_2024_7_P413_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P413 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
• Establishing or approving underwriting standards;

[gs_2024_7_P413_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P413 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
• Assessing the likelihood that a counterparty will default on its payment obligations;

[gs_2024_7_P413_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P413 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
• Measuring our current and potential credit exposure and losses resulting from a counterparty default;

[gs_2024_7_P413_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P413 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
• Using credit risk mitigants, including collateral and hedging; and

[gs_2024_7_P413_S007] Parent gs_2024_7_P413 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
• Maximizing recovery through active workout and restructuring of claims.

[gs_2024_7_P414_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P414 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
We also perform credit analyses, which incorporate initial and ongoing evaluations of the capacity and willingness of a counterparty to meet its financial obligations.

[gs_2024_7_P414_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P414 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
For substantially all of our credit exposures, the core of our process is an annual counterparty credit evaluation or more frequently if deemed necessary as a result of events or changes in circumstances.

[gs_2024_7_P414_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P414 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
We determine an internal credit rating for the counterparty by considering the results of the credit evaluations and assumptions with respect to the nature of and outlook for the counterparty's industry and the economic environment.

[gs_2024_7_P414_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P414 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
For collateralized loans, we also take into consideration collateral received or other credit support arrangements when determining an internal credit rating.

[gs_2024_7_P414_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P414 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
Senior personnel, with expertise in specific industries, inspect and approve credit reviews and internal credit ratings.

[gs_2024_7_P415_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P415 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process
Our risk assessment process may also include, where applicable, reviewing certain key metrics, including, but not limited to, delinquency status, collateral value, FICO credit scores and other risk factors.

[gs_2024_7_P416_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P416 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
Our credit risk management systems capture credit exposure to individual counterparties and on an aggregate basis to counterparties and their subsidiaries.

[gs_2024_7_P416_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P416 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Credit Risk Management Process > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
These systems also provide management with comprehensive information about our aggregate credit risk by product, internal credit rating, industry, country and region.

[gs_2024_7_P417_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P417 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Measures
We measure our credit risk based on the potential loss in the event of non-payment by a counterparty using current and potential exposure.

[gs_2024_7_P417_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P417 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Measures
For derivatives and securities financing transactions, current exposure represents the amount presently owed to us after taking into account applicable netting and collateral arrangements, while potential exposure represents our estimate of the future exposure that could arise over the life of a transaction based on market movements within a specified confidence level.

[gs_2024_7_P417_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P417 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Measures
Potential exposure also takes into account netting and collateral arrangements.

[gs_2024_7_P417_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P417 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Measures
For loans and lending commitments, the primary measure is a function of the notional amount of the position.

[gs_2024_7_P418_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P418 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Stress Tests
We conduct regular stress tests to calculate the credit exposures, including potential concentrations that would result from applying shocks to counterparty credit ratings or credit risk factors (e.g., currency rates, interest rates, equity prices).

[gs_2024_7_P418_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P418 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Stress Tests
These shocks cover a wide range of moderate and more extreme market movements, including shocks to multiple risk factors, consistent with the occurrence of a severe market or economic event.

[gs_2024_7_P418_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P418 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Stress Tests
In the case of sovereign default, we estimate the direct impact of the default on our sovereign credit exposures, changes to our credit exposures arising from potential market moves in response to the default, and the impact of credit market deterioration on corporate borrowers and counterparties that may result from the sovereign default.

[gs_2024_7_P418_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P418 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Stress Tests
Unlike potential exposure, which is calculated within a specified confidence level, stress testing does not generally assume a probability of these events occurring.

[gs_2024_7_P418_S005] Parent gs_2024_7_P418 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Stress Tests
We also perform firmwide stress tests.

[gs_2024_7_P418_S006] Parent gs_2024_7_P418 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Stress Tests
See "Overview and Structure of Risk Management" for information about firmwide stress tests.

[gs_2024_7_P419_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P419 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Stress Tests
To supplement these regular stress tests, as described above, we also conduct tailored stress tests on an ad hoc basis in response to specific events that we deem significant.

[gs_2024_7_P419_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P419 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Stress Tests
We also utilize these stress tests to estimate the indirect impact of certain hypothetical events on our country exposures, such as the impact of credit market deterioration on corporate borrowers and counterparties along with the shocks to the risk factors described above.

[gs_2024_7_P419_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P419 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Stress Tests
The parameters of these shocks vary based on the scenario reflected in each stress test.

[gs_2024_7_P419_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P419 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Stress Tests
We review estimated losses produced by the stress tests in order to understand their magnitude, highlight potential loss concentrations, and assess and seek to mitigate our exposures, where necessary.

[gs_2024_7_P420_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P420 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Limits
We use credit risk limits at various levels, as well as underwriting standards to manage the size and nature of our credit exposures.

[gs_2024_7_P420_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P420 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Limits

[gs_2024_7_P422_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P422 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Mitigants
To reduce our credit exposures on derivatives and securities financing transactions, we may enter into netting agreements with counterparties that permit us to offset receivables and payables with such counterparties.

[gs_2024_7_P422_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P422 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Mitigants
We may also reduce credit risk with counterparties by entering into agreements that enable us to obtain collateral from them on an upfront or contingent basis and/or to terminate transactions if the counterparty's credit rating falls below a specified level.

[gs_2024_7_P422_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P422 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Mitigants

[gs_2024_7_P422_S004] Parent gs_2024_7_P422 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Mitigants

[gs_2024_7_P423_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P423 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Mitigants
For loans and lending commitments, depending on the credit quality of the borrower and other characteristics of the transaction, we employ a variety of potential risk mitigants.

[gs_2024_7_P423_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P423 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Mitigants
Risk mitigants include collateral provisions, guarantees, covenants, structural seniority of the bank loan claims and, for certain lending commitments, provisions in the legal documentation that allow us to adjust loan amounts, pricing, structure and other terms as market conditions change.

[gs_2024_7_P423_S003] Parent gs_2024_7_P423 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Mitigants

[gs_2024_7_P424_S001] Parent gs_2024_7_P424 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Mitigants

[gs_2024_7_P424_S002] Parent gs_2024_7_P424 - Item 7 - Credit Risk Management > Risk Mitigants
